title: Modified inertia from resolved circular and noncircular MaNGA kinematics
hypothesis: A mass-independent positive kinetic action with a universal acceleration or frequency kernel predicts both circular and noncircular ionized-gas motion from baryons beyond strong ordinary morphology and frequency controls, and its noncircular response transfers unchanged to stellar motion.

discovery_policy.universal_gravity_track: Require one unchanged action-eligible inertia kernel and universal parameters to beat baryonic, structural, flexible, and ordinary frequency controls on circular and noncircular gas motion, transfer without kernel reselection to stellar noncircular motion, preserve a positive kinetic spectrum and local limit, and remain eligible for later relativistic and lensing completion.
discovery_policy.phenomenon_publication_track: Retain a reproducible relation between response-blind baryonic frequency ratios and noncircular kinematics beyond morphology and population controls even if it cannot be a complete relativistic gravity theory.

theory_sources.boundary: Known result that Galilei-invariant modified-inertia MOND actions of the relevant kind are strongly time-nonlocal and that circular-orbit solutions can be exact; the circular algebraic lane is an equivalence control, not a new theory.

Known time-nonlocal modified-inertia models with nonlocal conserved momentum, angular momentum, and energy and effects depending on frequency ratios and averaged acceleration; the finite kernels here are bounded projections, not implementations of the complete published models.

Known argument that noncircular motions can distinguish modified inertia from algebraic circular RAR and modified-gravity formulations; this experiment uses snapshot harmonics rather than full trajectories.

independence.rule: Reconstruct the Item 34 response-blind fresh pool, then exclude every Item 34 exploration or confirmation role and every additional neighbor within 60 arcseconds before disk cuts, roles, folds, MAPS downloads, source thresholds, or velocity access.

sample.stratification: median response-blind stellar mass crossed with median response-blind Sersic index after all predecessor, coordinate, SNR, disk-profile, and inclination cuts; 50 selected per cell with ten sealed confirmations

derived_predictors.enclosed_mass: Sersic enclosed stellar-mass proxy using regularized gammainc(2n,b_n*(r/Re)^(1/n)) with b_n fixed by gammaincinv(2n,0.5)
derived_predictors.baryonic_speed: sqrt(G*M_enclosed/r) using the response-blind stellar-mass proxy; no gas, halo, velocity, or lensing mass is inserted
derived_predictors.orbital_frequency: baryonic_speed/r converted from km/s/kpc to Gyr^-1
derived_predictors.mode_frequency_ratio: flux-amplitude-weighted mean of continuum m=1,2,3 harmonic numbers, defaulting to one when all amplitudes vanish
derived_predictors.stellar_age_proxy_gyr: clip(0.5+5*(Dn4000-1),0.1,10); a population clock proxy, not a measured formation age
derived_predictors.vertical_to_orbital_frequency: sqrt(4*pi*G*rho_global)/omega_b where rho_global=3*Mstar/(4*pi*Re^3); a source-only structural proxy, not a measured vertical oscillation

response.circular_amplitude: absolute c1 deprojected by the frozen photometric inclination for Halpha

physics.action_proxy: S_k=(m/2) integral d_omega K_ij(abs(omega),baryonic_invariants) v_i*(omega)v_j(omega), with real even frequency kernels and positive kinetic eigenvalues
physics.variation_proxy: K_ij a_j equals the baryonic force per unit mass; circular delta log10(v)=-0.5 log10(K_circ), while noncircular response uses the source-harmonic weighted ratio K_circ/K_mode
physics.conservation_proxy: real even frequency kernels, translation-independent velocity action, rotational scalar or symmetric baryon-covariant tensor, and positive kinetic eigenvalues; this establishes only a quadratic effective-action identity, not a relativistic stress tensor
physics.equivalence_principle_proxy: kernel is independent of tracer mass and composition; Halpha-to-stellar transfer tests but does not prove universality
physics.causality_boundary: an even time-nonlocal action is time symmetric and does not establish a causal initial-value formulation

candidate_generator.algorithm: PCG64 permutation of an exact mixed-radix grammar with 65536 raw cells in each of four modified-inertia niches

niches.operator: acceleration-only circular modified-inertia response with identical circular and harmonic kinetic factors
niches.equivalence: behaviorally indistinguishable from an algebraic modified-gravity/RAR rewrite on exactly circular motion

niches.operator: positive even frequency-domain kinetic kernel whose response differs between orbital harmonics
niches.equivalence: known nonlocal modified-inertia architecture with a newly bounded finite observational grammar

niches.operator: positive even spectral kernel coupled to a response-blind stellar-maturity proxy for eliminated slow degrees of freedom
niches.equivalence: combines known time-averaged inertia with a cross-sectional spectral-clock proxy; causal history is not observed

niches.operator: symmetric positive radial/tangential kinetic tensor built from baryonic density and orbital-frequency ratios
niches.equivalence: may overlap anisotropic modified gravity observationally; action placement and unchanged tracer transfer are the distinguishing commitments

equivalence_boundaries: Circular algebraic modified inertia is not distinguishable from a force-law rewrite on circular snapshots and is ineligible for a universal Item 35 pass.
Even spectral and history kernels instantiate known modified-inertia ideas; a selected parameter cell is not historical novelty.
The baryon-covariant tensor is only a potentially new synthesis until action-level and behavioral equivalence searches against anisotropic modified gravity are complete.
Snapshot harmonics are not full trajectories, vertical motions, eccentricity histories, or direct measurements of an inertia kernel.
Raw parameter cells are not independent laws; behavioral equivalence classes are counted separately and labels never prune.

evaluation.permutation_strategy: Freedman-Lane residual permutation around the ordinary frequency and morphology OOF prediction independently for circular and noncircular channels within response-blind mass-by-Sersic cells and annuli, with full candidate and baseline selection repeated
